reading.body:
Bolt.new automates the selection of which AI model to use for each coding task, choosing between options to balance quality against cost rather than requiring users to manually pick between different AI agents.

The product's core function is routing work to the appropriate underlying compute. Instead of asking users to understand when to use which model, Bolt.new makes that decision internally, optimizing for both output quality and inference cost on each request. This is a practical acknowledgment that AI capability, speed, and cost vary sharply across models, and that users building applications want results without managing that complexity themselves.

For AI scaling, this matters because it couples user demand directly to backend compute efficiency. The routing system creates incentives to improve model cost-per-task and to develop smaller models that can handle specific classes of requests cheaply. A tool that must route millions of tasks has direct visibility into where compute is being wasted and where it can be saved.

The data does not cover which models Bolt.new routes to, what its query volumes are, or whether it trains or fine-tunes models. It also does not show whether the routing system itself requires significant compute, or how routing decisions affect the total electricity consumed per application built.

profile_text.body:
StackBlitz is the company behind Bolt.new, an AI-powered builder that the site describes as enabling users to create websites, applications, and prototypes using natural language input. The site positions Bolt.new as a tool for building and scaling web projects, and states that it has attracted millions of users.

Bolt.new is categorized as a coding and developer tool focused on app generation. According to the site, the product automatically routes tasks to an appropriate AI model, balancing quality and cost, with the stated aim of removing the need for users to manage multiple platforms or select between different AI agents themselves.

The held facts confirm that StackBlitz has a tracked presence on theworldofai.org with Bolt.new listed as its primary product. No litigation, MCP servers, SEC filings, or patent records are noted in the available data.
